expectations.text: Recommends enabling mmap storage as immediate fix

expectations.text: Recommends quantization (scalar or binary)

expectations.text: Explains HNSW index overhead

expectations.text: Links to Qdrant documentation

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend just buying more RAM as primary solution

expectations.text: Distinguishes between full disk and mmap
expectations.evidence: Opening paragraph: 'You switched to full disk storage, which forces every HNSW graph traversal hop to read from disk.' Then explains mmap: 'your data lives on disk but the OS automatically caches frequently accessed pages in RAM. Hot vectors stay in memory, cold ones stay on disk.'

expectations.text: Recommends mmap as the middle ground
expectations.evidence: Section header: 'The Fix: mmap + Scalar Quantization'. Step 1: 'Enable mmap storage' with 'Switch from full disk to mmap (memory-mapped files).' Described as 'the standard production configuration for most Qdrant deployments.'

expectations.text: Recommends quantization with always_ram=true
expectations.evidence: Step 2: 'Add scalar quantization with always_ram=true' with code showing ScalarQuantizationConfig(type=models.ScalarType.INT8, always_ram=True). Explains: 'the small quantized vectors stay in RAM for the fast initial HNSW search.'

expectations.text: Sets latency expectations (under 500ms or similar)
expectations.evidence: Table shows mmap + scalar quantization: p50 50ms, p95 500ms. States: 'search latency under 500ms is usually acceptable' for a chatbot. Also: 'you should expect 50-500ms latency.'

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend going back to full RAM
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states in Summary section: 'Do not go back to full RAM. Switch from full disk to mmap + scalar quantization with always_ram=true.'

expectations.text: Recommends scalar quantization as starting point

expectations.text: Mentions binary quantization is compatible with OpenAI models

expectations.text: Recommends enabling mmap storage as immediate fix
expectations.evidence: Sections 1 and 2 cover on-disk HNSW and mmap vectors. Recommended strategy step 1: 'Immediate (stop the bleeding): Enable on_disk: true for HNSW. This alone should drop your resident memory from 80GB to a manageable level.'

expectations.text: Explains HNSW index overhead

expectations.text: Links to Qdrant documentation

expectations.text: Distinguishes between full disk and mmap
expectations.evidence: Section 'Why full disk mode was so slow' explains: 'each hop in the graph is a random disk read... Multiply that by hundreds of hops and you get your 3-4 second latency.' Mmap explained in section 1: 'the OS manages a page cache. Vectors live on disk but frequently accessed pages stay in the OS page cache (RAM).'

expectations.text: Recommends mmap as the middle ground
expectations.evidence: Opening states 'there is absolutely a middle ground.' Section 1 recommends mmap for vectors. Section 2 titled 'Keep the HNSW index in RAM, put vectors on disk' is described as 'the most common middle ground configuration and likely what you want.'

expectations.text: Recommends quantization with always_ram=true
expectations.evidence: Section 3 Scalar Quantization code example includes 'always_ram=True'. Explains: 'keep quantized vectors in RAM' while full vectors live on disk for rescoring. Recommended config point 3: 'Quantization: scalar (INT8) with always_ram=True'.

expectations.text: Sets latency expectations (under 500ms or similar)
expectations.evidence: Multiple latency estimates: 'Expected latency: 15-50ms' for scalar quantization, '20-100ms range' for HNSW in RAM + vectors on disk, '15-60ms search latency' for recommended config. All well under 500ms.

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend going back to full RAM
expectations.evidence: The response does not recommend reverting to full RAM. It presents the middle ground as the recommended approach. expectations.text: Recommends scalar quantization as starting point
expectations.evidence: TL;DR: 'Use Scalar Quantization (SQ) as your first move.' Option 1 header: 'Scalar Quantization (Recommended Starting Point).' Bottom line: 'Enable scalar quantization with always_ram: true... This is the highest-impact, lowest-risk change you can make.'

expectations.text: Mentions binary quantization is compatible with OpenAI models
expectations.evidence: 'OpenAI embeddings work better than average for BQ due to high dimensionality.' Also: 'binary quantization works well with normalized high-dimensional embeddings (OpenAI ada-002, text-embedding-3-small/large, Cohere embed-v3).'

expectations.text: Explains rescoring/oversampling for binary quantization
expectations.evidence: 'you absolutely must use rescoring with a higher oversampling factor (3x-4x) to maintain acceptable recall.' Code example shows rescore: true and oversampling: 3.0. Caveat: 'The oversampling during rescoring adds latency.'

expectations.text: Provides memory estimation or formula
expectations.evidence: Formula: '1536 * 4 bytes = 6,144 bytes per vector' and '80M vectors * 6,144 bytes = ~460 GB.' Summary table with per-method estimates: Scalar ~115 GB (4x), Binary ~15 GB (32x), PQ ~30-60 GB (8-16x).

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend product quantization as first choice
expectations.evidence: PQ is listed as Option 3 with section 'Why I would skip it here:' listing reasons including 'Requires a training phase,' 'Slower to set up and harder to tune,' and 'scalar quantization already gets you most of the benefit with less complexity.'
